notice.policy.purpose.title: Your local checks
notice.policy.purpose.body: Surfare checks messages, links, images and QR codes for warning signs. Local checks, image text reading and QR decoding run on your device. Results help you decide what to check next; they can sometimes miss details or misunderstand a message.
notice.policy.sharing.title: Checking links on your device
notice.policy.sharing.body: Link checks use local patterns and reference lists. When you press Check while connected, recognized shortened links in messages, web addresses, image text and QR codes are followed automatically through our server. Only each address goes to the linked sites and their HTTP redirect destinations; those sites may record the visit. Web addresses entered in the Links detector are followed when you press Check; other QR links have a separate destination-check button. No message or QR image is sent to these sites. Recognized private QR data and links containing credentials or access tokens are not followed. URL reputation services are not used. AI help has a separate sharing choice.
notice.policy.ai.title: Choosing online help
notice.policy.ai.body: AI help is optional and starts off. Turning it on lets the text you check (including text read from an image or QR code), result details, questions, language and up to eight recent chat messages go through Surfare's server. AI double-checks use OpenRouter and its selected model provider first, with Google Gemini as backup. Ask Surfy chat also uses OpenRouter first, with Google Gemini as backup. Online image detection is a separate choice: a smaller JPEG goes to Sightengine, without the original file or its metadata. Surfy receives text, not image bytes. Each provider has its own storage and data-use policy. With AI help off, Surfy uses local replies. Surfy Lifeguard has a separate AI double-check choice: your question, service name, country, selected situations and up to six recent chat messages go through our server to OpenRouter and its selected model provider, with Google Gemini as backup. It starts off, uses existing AI knowledge and does not browse the web. Local guidance works without it.
notice.policy.retention.title: What stays on your device
notice.policy.retention.body: Surfare does not save a history of your checks or chat. These stay in the current page session and clear when you reload or close it. Your language, privacy acknowledgment, offline app files and downloaded reports may stay on this device. Up to three items shared from another app can wait locally until opened. Unopened items expire after 10 minutes and are removed when accessed or on a later share. Feedback goes through EmailJS to the team, with the fields you enter, page address and send time; their own retention policies apply. Submissions and feedback are not automatically used for training.
notice.policy.security.title: A few simple precautions
notice.policy.security.body: Share only content you have permission to use. Leave out passwords, one-time codes and private access links. Surfare uses request checks and other safeguards to help protect information, though no app can promise perfect security.
notice.policy.rights.title: Your privacy rights
notice.policy.rights.body: Your rights under RA 10173, the Data Privacy Act, still apply. Where applicable, these include being informed, access, correction, objection, erasure or blocking, portability, damages, and raising a complaint with the National Privacy Commission, subject to the law. You can review or clear this acknowledgment anytime. Clearing it does not remove information already sent to another service; contact that service about its records. The official links below explain your rights.
notice.policy.terms.title: Using Surfare
notice.policy.terms.body: Use Surfare for content you are allowed to check. Results are a guide: a warning is not proof of wrongdoing, and low risk is not a guarantee. Confirm unexpected requests through a contact or app you already know. You can choose Not now and keep browsing; checks and the tour will ask you to review this notice first.
signal.violence: The message contains texts that show violence.
signal.extortion: The message tries to pressure you by demanding money or something else.
signal.blackmail: The message threatens to expose private information.
signal.intimidation: The message tries to scare or intimidate you.
signal.harassment: The message keeps targeting or bothering you.
signal.secret: The message asks you to keep something secret.
signal.advance-fee: The message asks for money first before giving something in return.
signal.investment: The message pushes an investment that may not be real.
signal.job-fee: The message asks you to pay to get a job or task.
signal.remote: The message asks for access to your device or account.
signal.personal: The message asks for private information.
signal.scam: The message looks like a trick to get money or information.
signal.other: Something in the message does not look right.
signalHelp.pressure: Pressure can make you decide before you have time to check. Pause and verify the request separately.
signalHelp.codes: Someone who gets your code may be able to sign in or approve a payment. Do not share it.
signalHelp.account: Sharing account details or access can let someone take over your account. Use the official app to check.
signalHelp.money: You could lose money if you pay before checking the offer. Verify who is asking and what you are paying for.
signalHelp.identity: A familiar name is easy to copy. Confirm the sender or full web address through the official app or website.
signalHelp.secrecy: Keeping it secret can stop someone you trust from spotting a problem. Ask them before acting.
signalHelp.address: This can hide where the link really goes. Check the full address before opening it or entering details.
signalHelp.weakAddress: This clue alone does not prove a scam. It only matters alongside the request and other warning signs.
signalHelp.pattern: Similar wording or addresses appeared in the reference data. Similarity can be wrong, so it is a clue rather than proof.
signalHelp.report: This finding is based on a regulator list or notice. Check the official notice and the exact service or web address.
ask.signalNotFound: That warning is not among the tags in this result. I can explain the highlighted phrases, but I should not say a warning was found when it was not.
ask.uncertain.answer: These checks can miss scams or flag a real message by mistake. The tags show clues, not proof. Confirm unexpected requests through an official app or a number you already trust.
signal.loan-fee: The offer asks for payment before releasing a loan.
signal.task-recruitment: The message offers easy earnings and asks you to contact a recruiter.
signal.cancel-lure: The message asks you to use a link to cancel an unexpected charge.
signal.benefit-claim: The message asks you to claim a benefit through a contact or link.
signal.load-transfer: The message asks you to dial a code that may transfer your load.
signal.guaranteed-winnings: The sender promises to make you win money.
signal.winnings-deposit: The sender asks for a cash-in or deposit in exchange for promised winnings.

result.imageMetadata.check.signature-val: The source note signature passed its check.
result.imageMetadata.check.signature-fai: The source note signature could not be validated.
result.imageMetadata.check.file-match: The source note matches this copy of the file.

result.sightengine.title: Sightengine image detection
result.sightengine.summary.high: We found signs that AI may have been used. This check can be wrong.
result.sightengine.summary.low: We didn't find clear signs of AI. This doesn't prove it's a real photo.
result.sightengine.summary.uncertain: The check couldn't tell if AI was used. The original image or its source may help.
result.sightengine.scoreHelp: Higher means a stronger AI-generation signal. This is not an accuracy percentage.
result.sightengine.limitation: Automated image detection can be wrong. Screenshots, recompression and edits can change the result. This check does not prove how the image was made.
result.sightengine.credentials: The image service rejected access. Contact Surfare support; local file notes are still available.
result.sightengine.quota: The online check has reached its limit. Please try again later.
result.sightengine.unsupported: We couldn't check this image online. Try another image.
result.imageSimple.fileAi: The file notes also mention AI use. See how we checked for more details.
result.imageSimple.next: Check the original source before trusting or sharing this image.
ask.imageLimits.answer: Yes. AI checks can miss AI images or flag real photos by mistake. Screenshots and edits can change the result, so check the original source if it matters.
ask.imageScore.answer: The score goes from 0 to 1. A higher number means the checker found more signs of AI. It isn't a percentage of how accurate the check is.
ask.imageScore.unavailable: There isn't an online score for this image yet. Try the online image check when it's available.

ask.clickedLink: I already clicked the link. What now?
ask.clickedLink.answer:
Close the page and avoid entering anything else.
- If you entered a password or code, secure that account through its official app.
- If something downloaded, update your device?s security software and run a scan.
ask.sharedSecret: I shared my code or password. What now?
ask.sharedSecret.answer:
Secure the account through its official app or website now.
- Change an exposed password, and change it anywhere else you reused it.
- Contact official support if you shared a code or see unfamiliar activity. Do not send me the code.
ask.sentMoney: I already sent money. What can I do?
ask.sentMoney.answer:
Contact your bank or payment provider immediately.
- Explain that you suspect a scam and ask whether the payment can be stopped or reversed. Recovery is not guaranteed.
- Keep the messages and receipts. Do not pay anyone who promises to recover the money for a fee.
ask.verifySender: How can I verify the sender?
ask.verifySender.answer:
Use a contact you find independently.
- Open the organization?s usual app or call a number you already trust.
- Ask whether they sent the request. Names, logos, and profile photos alone do not prove identity.
ask.reportSender: Should I block or report the sender?
ask.reportSender.answer:
If you suspect a scam, stop replying.
- Save the conversation if you need a record, then use the app?s report or block option.
- If money or account access is involved, contact your provider through official support too.
ask.imageScreenshot: Does a screenshot change the result?
ask.imageScreenshot.answer:
A screenshot may not keep the original file notes.
- Missing notes do not prove that an image is real or AI-made.
- An online image check can add clues, but it still cannot confirm authenticity.
ask.imageVerify: How can I check where this image came from?
ask.imageVerify.answer:
Look for the original source before sharing.
- Ask for the original file or search for earlier copies of the image.
- Compare the original date and context. A detector result alone does not verify the story.

recovery.label: Surfy Lifeguard
recovery.title: Let's take it one step at a time.
recovery.launchBody: A little guidance when something feels wrong.
recovery.resultAction: Already clicked or sent money? Surfy Lifeguard can guide you
recovery.intro: Something didn't feel right? Tell me what happened and we'll make the next steps a little clearer.
recovery.planTitle: Here is where you can start.
recovery.planIntro: Take the steps that fit your situation. You can ask Surfy if you need a little more help.
recovery.multiple: Pick what fits. It is okay if you are not sure.
recovery.situation.shared: I shared a password, PIN, OTP, or account details
recovery.situation.paid: I sent money or noticed an unauthorized payment
recovery.situation.threatened: Someone is threatening or blackmailing me
recovery.situation.danger: Someone is in immediate physical danger
recovery.situation.unsure: I am not sure what happened
recovery.privacy: Your checklist stays on this device. You choose whether to use online AI help.
recovery.outside: These hotline numbers are for the Philippines, so they are hidden here. Contact your local emergency services for immediate danger, and use your provider's official app or website for account help.
recovery.contactIntro: Use these official channels, not contact details from the suspicious message.
recovery.contact.emergency: For immediate danger to someone's physical safety in the Philippines. Do not wait to finish this checklist.
recovery.contact.gcash: 2882 is for Globe/TM subscribers. Urgent scam, fraud, and unauthorized-transaction support is available 24/7. Other networks can use the official Help Center's internet-call or chat options.
recovery.contact.maya: Maya app support: daily 8 AM to 7 PM, with after-hours assistance for emergencies such as suspected unauthorized transactions.
recovery.contact.bank: Contact the bank or payment provider using its official app, your card, or a number you already trust. Report the incident there first. BSP guidance explains escalation if it remains unresolved.
recovery.contact.cicc: Philippine cybercrime and online-scam reporting. For payment incidents, contact your bank or e-wallet first; CICC does not replace its fraud support.
recovery.step.safety.title: Put physical safety first
recovery.step.safety.body: Move to a safer place if you can and contact local emergency services. Reach a trusted person. Do not wait for Surfare or a scam report to resolve immediate danger.
recovery.step.payment.title: Report the payment to your provider now
recovery.step.payment.body: Ask whether the payment can be stopped or disputed and whether your account needs protection. Keep the case reference number. Recovery is not guaranteed; do not pay a recovery fee to a stranger.
recovery.step.account.title: Secure the affected account
recovery.step.account.body: Use the official app or website from a device you trust. Change an exposed password, including reused copies, review active sessions, and contact support if you shared an OTP or PIN. Never give Surfare your code.
recovery.step.device.title: Check your device
recovery.step.device.body: Do not open an unfamiliar download. If you installed something, update your device's security software and run a scan. Avoid banking on a device you suspect is compromised; get trusted technical help if needed.
recovery.step.stop.title: Stop interacting with the suspicious page or sender
recovery.step.stop.body: Close the page. Do not enter more information, approve requests, or send more money. Opening a link alone does not establish what information, if any, was exposed.
recovery.step.review.title: Check what you actually did
recovery.step.review.body: Did you type a password, approve a code, make a payment, or install an app? Change your answers if you remember more. Check account activity through the official app, not the suspicious link.
recovery.step.evidence.title: Keep a private record
recovery.step.evidence.body: Keep the messages, relevant screenshots, receipts, and transaction references for official support. Do not share passwords or OTPs. This downloaded plan does not contain those details.
recovery.step.threat.title: Get support for the threat
recovery.step.threat.body: Reach a trusted person and report the threat through official cybercrime or police channels. Preserve the messages. If physical danger becomes immediate, use local emergency services.
recovery.step.report.title: Report through the relevant official channel
recovery.step.report.body: Use your provider's fraud process for account or payment issues and the platform's report tools for abusive accounts. In the Philippines, CICC can receive cybercrime reports. Keep any reference numbers.
recovery.limit: A guide to your options, one step at a time. Your provider can confirm what is possible.
recovery.rates: Availability can change. Short codes are Philippine numbers; carrier charges may apply. Calls and websites open only when you choose them.
signal.gift-card-prize-fee: A prize offer asks you to buy a gift card or send its code.
signal.unsolicited-work-offer: A paid-work selection directs you to an unverified link.
signal.parcel-update-link: Delivery details are requested through an unfamiliar website.
signal.account-alert-link: A banking or wallet alert directs you outside the listed official sites.

notice.reachedEnd: You have reached the end. You can now tick the box.

ask.onlinePrivacy: About the AI double-check and privacy
ask.helpInfo.title: About the AI double-check
ask.helpInfo.what: The AI double-check gives your check a second look and helps Surfy answer your questions. It needs internet and can sometimes miss details.
ask.helpInfo.privacy: When it is on, your checked text, result details, questions and recent chat are sent to online AI services. Surfare does not save a check history; those services follow their own data policies.
ask.helpInfo.choice: You can turn it off anytime. Image checks have a separate choice.
ask.helpInfo.chatWhat: AI chat help lets Surfy explain your image result and answer follow-up questions. It needs internet and does not change the image check.
ask.helpInfo.chatPrivacy: Surfy receives written check details, your questions and recent chat, not your photo. Surfare does not save a check history; online services follow their own data policies.
recovery.providerHint: e.g. BPI, UnionBank, PayPal or Facebook
recovery.providerOptional: A service name is enough. No account numbers, passwords or codes needed.
recovery.chat.title: Ask Surfy
recovery.chat.subtitle: A little help with what comes next.
recovery.chat.offline: You are offline. The checklist and local tips still work.
recovery.chat.greeting: I'm here to help you work out what to do next. Tell me what happened, or pick a question below.
recovery.chat.unavailable: Surfy's online help is unavailable. Here is a general next step instead:
recovery.chat.privacy: No passwords or codes needed. This conversation clears when you close Surfy Lifeguard. Online services have their own data policies.
recovery.chat.prompt.contact: How do I find the right support?
recovery.chat.clarify: Choose what happened on the checklist so I can suggest a general next step. For more specific questions, add the service name and turn on the AI double-check.
recovery.chat.localContact: Start with Help or Support inside the app you normally use. For a bank card, use the contact printed on the card. Add the service name and enable the AI double-check for more guidance.
recovery.chat.onlineInfo: Surfy can tailor the next steps to your situation. Uses AI knowledge, without live web browsing.
recovery.chat.inviteBody: Ask a question in your own words.

qr.title: About this QR code
qr.offline: Connect to the internet to check this link.
qr.privacy: Checking a short link contacts that website and follows its HTTP redirects. Other links are contacted only when you choose to check their destination. Websites may record the visit. No QR image is uploaded.
qr.summary: Check where this link goes before opening it.
qr.warningSummary: We found warning signs in this link. Pause before opening it.
qr.limitation: Each recorded address is checked with local rules and reference lists. This is not a live reputation lookup or proof of safety. JavaScript, HTML refreshes, browser-specific redirects and page content are not checked. AI double-checks do not follow links.
qr.payload.text: This QR contains text. We checked it for warning signs.
qr.payload.private: This QR contains private details. They stay on your device, and we cannot verify them here.
qr.payload.unsupported: This QR contains an action we can't check. Only use it if you trust where it came from.
qr.reason.blocked_target: This target was not contacted: private networks, embedded credentials or access tokens, non-web protocols and unusual ports are blocked.
qr.reason.redirect_loop: The link repeats a previous address. The redirect check stopped.
qr.reason.redirect_limit: The redirect limit was reached. The complete destination could not be verified.
qr.reason.missing_location: The website returned a redirect without a destination address.
qr.reason.invalid_redirect: The website returned an invalid redirect address.
qr.reason.http_error: The website refused the request or returned an error. The destination could not be verified.
qr.reason.timeout: The destination did not finish responding in time.
qr.reason.network: The destination could not be reached. Existing local warnings still apply.
qr.reason.rate_limit: Too many destination checks are running. Wait a moment and try again.
qr.reason.service_unavailable: Destination checking is unavailable on this server. Local QR checks still work.
qr.reason.invalid_request: The QR destination request was invalid. Scan the code again.
qr.reason.origin: This page cannot use the destination service. Refresh and try again.
qr.reason.method: The destination request could not be processed.
qr.direct: Direct URL; no HTTP redirect observed
qr.priorWarning: An earlier check found warning signs; the failed retry does not clear them.
qr.simple.ready: This QR contains a website link
qr.simple.checked: We found where this link goes
qr.simple.before: Check its destination before deciding whether to open it.
qr.simple.avoid: Avoid opening it. Use the service's usual app or website instead.
qr.simple.confirm: Make sure this is the website you expected. Finding it does not prove it is safe.
qr.simple.tryLater: We couldn't confirm where it goes. Check with the sender before opening it.
qr.simple.blocked: Don't open it unless you trust where it came from.
qr.simple.sharing: This contacts the linked websites. They may record the visit.
qr.simple.earlierWarning: We couldn't recheck it. Earlier warnings still apply.
qr.simple.checkedSummary: We found its destination. This does not prove the website is safe.
destination.title: Where the link goes
destination.ready: This is the link we found
destination.privacy: This destination check sends only the selected address through Surfare to the linked websites. They may record the visit. It does not send your full message.
destination.checkingBody: We are following the short link and checking the addresses along the way.
destination.beforeCheck: Checking follows short links online. Websites may record the visit. This link check sends the address, not your full message.
qr.reason.hidden_destination: We couldn't reveal the final website. This short link needs a browser or did not provide a redirect.
destination.linkBeforeCheck: Checking contacts this website and follows redirects. Websites may record the visit.
destination.addressChecked: The redirects were checked; the page content was not.
